finding: Deloitte India's 2026 campus survey reports that 35% of organisations say AI adoption is creating new entry-level roles or skill requirements (up from 21% the year before), and that 86% say AI or agentic AI is transforming their recruitment process.
implication: Employers are screening with AI and want AI-literate graduates, so expect automated assessments and make your public work easy to find and verify.

source.name: Deloitte India, Campus Workforce Trends 2026 press release

finding: The same Deloitte India study says employers increasingly use internships as a predictor of long-term success, with 80% maintaining dedicated campus hiring teams and technology remaining students' most preferred sector for the fifth year.
implication: Treat internships and pre-placement offers as the main entry route, and start applying in your second or third year.

source.name: Deloitte India, Campus Workforce Trends 2026 press release

finding: A campus-hiring report from Unstop says 87.8% of companies were actively recruiting on campus, yet 84% of undergraduates remained unplaced, and that AI/ML skills appear in 60-70% of fresher job descriptions, including some non-technical roles.
figure: 87.8% recruiting vs 84% unplaced; AI/ML in 60-70% of fresher JDs
implication: Demand exists but placement depends on demonstrable skill. AI/ML literacy is becoming a baseline expectation even outside AI roles.

source.name: Unstop, The State of Campus Hiring in India 2026
